script.title: How Does a Cat Always Land on Its Feet?

voice_performance.performance_intent: A calm, curious climb: each rung a little brighter, a surprise at 'sitting still', quiet awe at light, then a dry finished close.
voice_performance.energy_curve: s1 building; s2 surprise; s3 impressed; s4 awe -> explanation; s5 calm, dry, resolved.
voice_performance.pause_policy: Gaps widened at the foundation for a >= 45 s film (lesson 48); ~1.5 s settle after s5 on the resolved chord.

provider_notes.elevenlabs: Bella hpp4J3VqNfWAUOO0d1Us, eleven_v4 tags in delivery_cues.provider_text. ONE take per section; retake only if Whisper QA fails; max 2. Check baked-in pauses (lesson 29) and the last word 'way' level (lesson 30).

sections.label: Hook - the first rungs
sections.text: You walk at about five kilometres an hour. A cheetah sprints at about a hundred. A diving falcon hits nearly four hundred.
sections.speaker_directions: Curious and clear; three quick steps up, each a little brighter.

delivery_cues.provider_text: [curious] You walk at about five kilometres an hour. A cheetah sprints at about a hundred. A diving falcon hits nearly four hundred.

enhancement_cues.description: Log rail: marker climbs WALK -> CHEETAH (window S1)

sections.label: Sound, and you
sections.text: Sound outruns them all at over twelve hundred. But sitting still, you're doing over a hundred thousand, riding Earth around the Sun.
sections.speaker_directions: Pleased on 'twelve hundred'; a turn on 'But sitting still' - a little surprise.

delivery_cues.provider_text: Sound outruns them all at over twelve hundred. [surprised] But sitting still, you're doing over a hundred thousand, riding Earth around the Sun.

sections.label: Our fastest machine
sections.text: The fastest thing we've ever built, the Parker Solar Probe, reached nearly seven hundred thousand, falling toward the Sun.
sections.speaker_directions: Proud but plain; 'falling toward the Sun' lighter.

delivery_cues.provider_text: The fastest thing we've ever built, the Parker Solar Probe, reached nearly seven hundred thousand, [lightly] falling toward the Sun.

enhancement_cues.description: Window S3 Parker Solar Probe (AI impression)

sections.label: Light, and the wall
sections.text: Light does over a billion. And nothing with mass can catch it: the closer you get, the more energy each step costs, without end.
sections.speaker_directions: Quiet awe on 'over a billion'; then clear and steady through the explanation.

delivery_cues.provider_text: [awed] Light does over a billion. And nothing with mass can catch it: the closer you get, the more energy each step costs, without end.

enhancement_cues.description: LIGHT at the top; red 'c' wall line

sections.label: Never all the way - finished close
sections.text: The Large Hadron Collider pushes protons to within a hair of light speed. Close. But never all the way.
sections.speaker_directions: Calm; 'Close.' a soft beat; the last sentence slow and dry, falling to a finished cadence on 'way'.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: End on a falling, finished cadence; keep 'way' clear (lesson 30).
delivery_cues.provider_text: The Large Hadron Collider pushes protons to within a hair of light speed. [softly] Close. [dryly] But never all the way.

enhancement_cues.description: marker stops just under the wall; settle

ending_details.rule: User's standing rule (d-003): end on a finished line.
ending_details.closing_line: Close. But never all the way.
ending_details.after_last_word: Resolved chord ~0.15 s after 'way'; the marker still just under the wall; ~1.5 s hold. No SFX under the closing sentence; duck deeper from 'But' (lesson 44); 'way' >= +12 dB over the bed (300-4000 Hz) and within ~3 dB of its sentence; 0.6 s end fade (lesson 43). build_soundtrack writes ending.closing_min_margin_db (lesson 49).

honesty_meter.MEASURED: measured, or an established finding stated simply

fact_notes: 'about a hundred' = cheetah 95 (wild, collar) to 103 km/h (track)
'nearly four hundred' = peregrine dive ~386-390 km/h, weakly sourced -> PROBABLY
'over twelve hundred' = 343 m/s in 20 C air = 1,235 km/h
'over a hundred thousand' = Earth's orbit 29.78 km/s = 107,200 km/h
'nearly seven hundred thousand' = Parker 430,000 mph = 692,000 km/h (Dec 2024)
'within a hair' = LHC protons 0.999999991 c (shown on screen as 99.9999991 %)
